Latest Labour and Social Insurance Law Changes in the GCC

We review the laws regularly and update the calculators as soon as a change takes effect. This is a short log of what changed, newest first.

Prepared and reviewed by the Mustahaqati team · Last updated: 2026-11-03

2026

DateCountryWhat changedCalculator
30 Oct 2026UAEThe ministry calls on companies with 50 or more workers to add another 1% of Emiratis in skilled jobs before 31 December 2026 (10% cumulative), with a contribution of AED 10,000 a month (AED 120,000 for the year) per missing Emirati.Emiratisation calculator
25–26 Oct 2026Saudi ArabiaThe wage needed to count a Saudi fully in Nitaqat rises to SAR 5,000 from 25 April 2027 and SAR 6,000 from 25 April 2028 (SAR 4,000 today). New electricity and water tariffs apply from 1 January 2027, with SAR 500 a month of support for eligible people.Nitaqat · Electricity · Water
Aug 2026UAESmall business relief from corporate tax (revenue up to AED 3 million) extended to tax periods ending by 31 December 2029, by Ministerial Decision 131 of 2026.Corporate tax
25 Jul 2026QatarLaw 9 of 2026 takes effect, amending the non-compete, disputes, strike and joint committee articles. No change to leave or end-of-service gratuity.Qatar gratuity
19 Jul 2026OmanThe sick leave insurance branch starts and covers non-Omanis: the employer pays the first 7 days and the fund reimburses the rest. The worker's entitlement is unchanged.Oman leave
1 Jul 2026UAECollection starts for first-half 2026 Emiratisation shortfalls, and Emiratis paid less than AED 6,000 a month no longer count towards targets; the company's new permits are suspended until it is corrected.Emiratisation calculator
1 Jul 2026Saudi ArabiaThe pension contribution for new entrants (insured since 3 July 2024) rises to 10% each for employee and employer, continuing up by half a point a year to 11% in 2028.GOSI contributions
22 Jun 2026OmanDecision R/12/2026: the old-age pension is due on reaching the age together with the end of service; anyone who keeps working is paid from the date service ends.Oman pension

2022–2024

DateCountryWhat changedCalculator
3 Jul 2024Saudi ArabiaThe new social insurance system takes effect: age 65 for new entrants, 2.25% per year on the average of the highest wages over 180 months, and transitional age tables for existing members.Pension · Retirement age

Widely reported changes that have not happened

  • Kuwait — 35 days of leave: a 2019 proposal that was never issued; 30 working days have applied since Law 85/2017.
  • UAE — longer private-sector maternity leave: under study since May 2025; the minimum is still 60 days.
  • Saudi Arabia — dependent fee change: the Ministry of Finance said in 2024 the fee was under review, but no decision was issued, so it remains SAR 400 a month per person.
  • Oman — savings scheme for non-Omanis: a 9% contribution replacing gratuity has not started yet; its start date is no later than 19 July 2027.

We follow the official gazette in each country. To compare entitlements across the region, see the GCC end-of-service comparison and the GCC pension comparison. Prefer Arabic? Use the Arabic version.

Frequently asked questions

Did Saudi end-of-service pay change with the 2025 amendments?

No. Articles 84, 85 and 87 were not amended, so the award and the resignation fractions are unchanged. But resignation is now defined for fixed-term contracts, and Article 79 bis regulates its acceptance within 30 days.

Has annual leave in Kuwait risen to 35 days?

No. The latest law in force is Law 85 of 2017: 30 working days, excluding weekly rest days and public holidays. The 35-day proposal was never issued.

Did Qatar's 2026 labour law amendments change leave or gratuity?

No. Law 9 of 2026, in force from 25 July 2026, amended the non-compete, disputes, strike and joint committee articles, and did not touch leave or end-of-service gratuity.

How do I know a calculator is up to date?

Every page shows its last update date under the title and cites the article of law and its official source at the end.
